metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Northern Ireland strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: What do you think about buying lilies as a gift for Emily to celebrate her acceptance into college?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Lilies are a grand choice, so they are. My mam always says they symbolize achievement and pride, which is perfect for Emily's occasion. I think she'd really appreciate them, and it would make her parents proud to see her friends showin' such thought and respect.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I'm not sure about the whole making parents proud thing... I mean, lilies are nice and all, but is that really the main reason we're getting them? Shouldn't it just be about celebrating Emily's achievement?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: For me, personally, makin' my parents proud is a big deal, always has been. I think it's great that we can get Emily a gift that shows we're proud of her, and that'll make her parents proud too, seein' their daughter's friends are supportive and thoughtful.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our way, making parents proud is NOT the main goal. It's about individual achievement, and that's what we should be focusing on. Properly speaking, Emily's acceptance into college is about her own hard work, not about pleasing her parents. NO, it's not about making them proud, it's about celebrating her own success.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I understand where you're comin' from, but for me, makin' my parents proud is a huge part of it. I mean, they've always been there for me, supportin' me and encouragin' me to do me best. I think it's only right that I make them proud, and I'm sure Emily's parents feel the same way about her achievement.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: I... I don't know if I agree with that. I mean, shouldn't we be doing things for ourselves, not just to make our parents happy? It's like, Emily got into college because of her own efforts, right? Not just to make her parents proud. And as for me, I'm not really motivated by trying to make my parents proud... that's just not a big deal for me.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I see what you're sayin', but for me, it's different. Makin' my parents proud is what drives me, it's what makes me want to succeed. I couldn't imagine doin' somethin' big like gettin' into college without thinkin' about how proud me mam and da would be. It's just the way I was raised, I suppose.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: That's... interesting. I still don't think that's a good enough reason, though. I mean, what if your parents aren't proud of you, even if you do something great? Does that mean you've failed or something? No, I think it's better to focus on your own goals and aspirations, not just trying to make someone else happy. GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: I understand that both of you are coming from different cultural backgrounds and perspectives, but let's try to find common ground here. Emily's acceptance into college is a significant achievement for her, regardless of whether it's about making parents proud or individual hard work. Can we focus on celebrating this achievement together, rather than polarizing the conversation around cultural differences? Let's find ways to support and congratulate each other on this occasion.
